variance_matched_null_check.purpose: round-1 next_round_priorities #3: was null_vs_real_sn_H1 > model_vs_real_sn_H1 a bounding-box artifact of the uniform-box null? This control uses a null matched to the model cloud's own per-axis variance instead.
variance_matched_null_check.conclusion: Ordering does NOT survive variance-matching -- round-1's null_vs_real_sn_H1 > model_vs_real_sn_H1 finding WAS a bounding-box artifact; no model-vs-real topology preference is supported.

predicted_topology_naive.naive_reading: If persistence-diagram 'dimension' tracked parameter count directly, going 6->5 params should show up as SOME detectable shrinkage of the observable-image's complexity/spread relative to round 1's model cloud.
predicted_topology_naive.status: This naive reading is NOT what round 1 found and is not what we predict here. It is recorded only because the task text states it verbatim.

predicted_topology_corrected.source: round-1 tda_report.json interpretation_caveat, carried forward unchanged: 'Betti numbers of the model cloud (beta0=1, beta1=beta2=0 expected for a smooth image of a box) are NOT a parameter count. They describe global shape (one connected contractible blob) which is uninformative about effective dimension here.'
predicted_topology_corrected.prediction_betti: H0=1 (single connected component), H1=0 in the persistent-forever sense (beta1 as reported by gudhi.betti_numbers()), IDENTICAL to round 1's model cloud [1,0], because a_pot,b_pot,mu_sym,lambda_sym,c4_pta_product are all still CONTINUOUS free parameters (none frozen to a point) -- removing one exactly-degenerate direction from a smooth map does not change the topology of a still-continuous, still-connected image. Betti numbers would only collapse toward a single point (beta0=1 with a near-zero-radius cloud, not a qualitatively different beta1=0 since that is already 0) if free parameters were fixed to specific numbers, i.e. genuinely reduced to zero, which has not happened this round (5 remain).
predicted_topology_corrected.prediction_effective_dimension_svd: The Jacobian-SVD effective dimension (jacobian_report.json's own diagnostic, NOT Betti numbers) should remain 3, unchanged from round 1's best_fit probe (singular values [4.65,2.58,1.72,3.7e-4,3.2e-14,0.0], eff_dim_at_1e-3=3). The removed direction (pta_suppression vs c4_c0_ratio difference) was ALREADY an exact SV=0.0 null direction in the 6-param model, so collapsing it to 1 parameter should not add or remove effective dimension: 5 nominal params, same 3 effective.
predicted_topology_corrected.prediction_bottleneck_vs_round1_model: NONZERO but small, NOT a topology change. Two independent sources of nonzero bottleneck distance are predicted, neither indicating 'more' or 'less' theory content: (a) a different RNG seed (43 vs 42) and a different sweep sample; (b) a genuinely different marginal density along the c4_pta_product/max_deviation_from_hd axis -- round 1's 6-dim LHS gives c4_c0_ratio*pta_suppression the density of a SUM of two independent log-uniform variables (a triangular-in-log distribution), whereas a fresh log-uniform draw directly on c4_pta_product gives a different (uniform-in-log) density on the same support. This is a sampling-density artifact, pre-registered here so a nonzero number below is not misread as evidence of a topology change.
predicted_topology_corrected.prediction_bottleneck_vs_real_sn: Should be of the same order as round 1's model_vs_real_sn_H1=0.0195 (within the sampling noise discussed above), since the sector that changed (PTA) is not one of the 4 embedding coordinates GUDHI's round-1 real_sn comparison actually used from the model side except through c4_pta_product/max_deviation_from_hd, which round 1's Jacobian already showed carries very weak signal (SV~3.7e-4) relative to the dominant a_pot/b_pot/mu_sym directions.
